prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: ISO 3166-1 current codes (first 14) (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 15 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "English short name (using title case)" · longest unbreakable unit 82px · widest one-line content 261px
  col 2: header "Alpha-2 code" · longest unbreakable unit 49px · widest one-line content 97px
  col 3: header "Alpha-3 code" · longest unbreakable unit 49px · widest one-line content 97px
  col 4: header "Numeric code" · longest unbreakable unit 61px · widest one-line content 100px
  col 5: header "Link to ISO 3166-2" · longest unbreakable unit 44px · widest one-line content 134px
  col 6: header "Independent" · longest unbreakable unit 91px · widest one-line content 91px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 360px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). At 360px some words cannot fit unsplit. Horizontal scrolling is ALLOWED: the table may be wider than 360px (column widths summing to more than 359px) (the reader scrolls), or you may fit within 359px and accept the consequences. Fitting and scrolling layouts are judged as two separate classes; propose good layouts of BOTH kinds.
Rendering convention: a full render shows the WHOLE table; anything right of the dashed box is not clipped — it is reached by scrolling. Where a layout scrolls, an extra "viewport view" image shows only what is visible at first sight.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Provide a reference for finding the current ISO 3166-1 codes and independence status of each listed country or territory.","tasks":["Find a country or territory by name and read across its row to retrieve a code or status.","Compare alpha-2, alpha-3 or numeric codes down a column, preserving leading zeros.","Use the ISO 3166-2 link associated with a country or territory.","Scan the alphabetical list sequentially and distinguish independent from non-independent entries."],"relations":["Each row binds one name to its alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric identifiers, subdivision link and independence status.","The alpha-2 code also appears at the end of the corresponding ISO 3166-2 link.","The three code columns are parallel identifiers, while the link and independence columns provide related information."],"roles":["The first column identifies the row and anchors lookup, even though no row headers are declared.","The three code columns support precise lookup and comparison.","The link column points to subdivision codes; the final column records a binary status.","Column headers distinguish similar identifiers and must remain understandable when wrapped."],"keep_whole":["Alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes and three-digit numeric codes, including leading zeros.","ISO 3166-2 link identifiers, where available width permits.","Individual words in names and headers, especially Independent, where available width permits."],"may_wrap":["Multiword country and territory names at spaces.","Headers between words, keeping Alpha-2, Alpha-3 and ISO 3166-2 recognizable."],"same_scale":["Alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have similar widths because their roles and content lengths are similar.","The numeric code column can be comparable in scale to the alpha columns; the name and link columns need more room for longer content."],"h_vs_v":"A 359px table forces some words or identifiers to split and increases row height, but keeps all columns in the initial view. A wider table preserves semantic units and reduces vertical disruption, while requiring horizontal scrolling and making it harder to keep the name visible alongside rightmost values."}
